sections.title: Habitat and size
sections.text: Common duckweed is a tiny floating plant of still water, often nutrient-rich. Its flattened oval fronds are about 1–8 mm long and float singly or in small groups.

sections.title: Roots and reproduction
sections.text: Each frond normally bears a single hanging root, which can reach about 15 cm. Flowering is rare; the plant reproduces mainly by budding new fronds. The fruit is about 0.8–1 mm long.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: The references consulted do not establish a reliable food use for this species. Avoid harvesting plants from polluted water.
